Confirming the version question with source, since it gates the upgrade decision: the gate is **unchanged between v2026.8.1 and v2026.9.2** — `src/plugins/compat/conversation-read-tools.ts` is byte-identical across both tags (same single-entry `HOST_RESTRICTED_CONVERSATION_READ_TOOLS = {"feishu:feishu_chat"}` set, same `entry.origin === "bundled" && manifestPlugin?.origin === "bundled"` exemption), and the only assembly-layer change in the range is a manifest-lookup refactor around the `blocksHostRestrictedConversationReadRegistration` call site, not a policy change. So if a Feishu-channel deployment hits this on 8.1, expect the same behavior on 9.2 — treat 9.2 upgrade as gated on a fix, not on the bump.

One extra data point against the fix design @itanyplus suggested (assembly-layer fix protecting other host-restricted plugins): the restriction list is currently a **single hardcoded pair** (`feishu:feishu_chat`), so today the blast radius is exactly this one tool — but the exemption requires *both* the registration entry and the manifest record to carry `origin === "bundled"`. `@openclaw/feishu` ships inside `extensions/` in the monorepo, yet a registration coming through the npm-install path can still end up with `entry.origin !== "bundled"` — which is precisely the "works bundled, breaks from npm" axis from my earlier comment. Worth deciding explicitly whether `extensions/*` shipped by this repo should be origin-trusted by definition (one-line policy change in `isBundledConversationReadToolRegistration`) rather than requiring both flags to line up.

Also +1 on the loud WARN when a registered entry is dropped — and note the dropping happens per-registration (13 tools in one entry here), so the warning should name the *gate* and the *plugin*, not just one tool name, or multi-tool plugins will still look partially healthy.
